newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan's new PM Majali holds first cabinet meeting.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's new PM Majali holds first cabinet meeting.

text.p: Jordan's new Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali held the first cabinet meeting on Thursday of a new technocratic government picked to run the country until elections due to be held by November, officials said.
Prime ministry officials quoted Majali as telling his 23 ministers about the "importance" of working to improve services to citizens and attaining stability and prosperity.
Majali stressed to his team the government would work hand in hand with "citizens in a participatory role with society within a framework of responsible freedom".

Majali was chosen by King Hussein after Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti tendered his resignation on Wednesday in an abrupt move that political observers tied to differences over handling of Israel ties after the killing of seven Israeli school girls by a lone Jordanian soldier last week.

Majali reviewed with his team the broad outlines of the new government's policy, whose priorities include cutting bloated bureacracy, alleviating poverty and pursuing free-market reforms including privatisation.

While the new cabinet includes high calibre technocrats with wide experience in government service, many analysts doubt the Majali government will take radical steps to tackle the country's chronic problems.

But the fact the new cabinet is surrounded by members of Jordan negotiating team who were involved in peace talks with Israel reflects the king's priority to push ahead with normalising ties with the country's powerful neighbour.
Majali was the leader of Jordan's negotiating team with Israel and as prime minister in 1994 signed the peace treaty between the two countries.
